title: How to stay calm under pressure - Noa Kageyama and Pen-Pen Chen

blocks.en_text: Your favorite athlete closes in for a victorious win.
blocks.zh_text: 你最喜欢的运动员逼近胜利的一刻。

blocks.en_text: The crowd holds its breath,
blocks.zh_text: 全场观众屏住呼吸，

blocks.en_text: and, at the crucial moment, she misses the shot.
blocks.zh_text: 可就在这关键时刻，她投偏了。

blocks.en_text: That competitor just experienced the phenomenon known as "choking,"
blocks.zh_text: 这位选手刚刚经历了一种现象，叫做“发挥失常”，

blocks.en_text: where despite months, even years, of practice,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是尽管练习了几个月、甚至几年，

blocks.en_text: a person fails right when it matters most.
blocks.zh_text: 一个人偏偏在最要紧的时候掉了链子。

blocks.en_text: Choking is common in sports,
blocks.zh_text: 发挥失常在体育中很常见，

blocks.en_text: where performance often occurs under intense pressure
blocks.zh_text: 因为运动表现往往是在巨大压力下产生的

blocks.en_text: and depends on key moments.
blocks.zh_text: 而且取决于关键时刻。

blocks.en_text: And yet, performance anxiety also haunts public speakers,
blocks.zh_text: 然而，表现焦虑也困扰着演讲者、

blocks.en_text: contestants in spelling bees,
blocks.zh_text: 拼字比赛的参赛者，

blocks.en_text: and even world-famous musicians.
blocks.zh_text: 甚至世界著名的音乐家。

blocks.en_text: Most people intuitively blame it on their nerves,
blocks.zh_text: 大多数人凭直觉把原因归咎于紧张，

blocks.en_text: but why does being nervous undermine expert performance?
blocks.zh_text: 但紧张为什么会削弱高手的表现呢？

blocks.en_text: There are two sets of theories,
blocks.zh_text: 有两类理论，

blocks.en_text: which both say that primarily, choking under pressure boils down to focus.
blocks.zh_text: 它们都认为，压力下的发挥失常主要归结于注意力。

blocks.en_text: First, there are the distraction theories.
blocks.zh_text: 第一类是分心理论。

blocks.en_text: These suggest that performance suffers when the mind is preoccupied
blocks.zh_text: 这类理论认为，当大脑被

blocks.en_text: with worries, doubts, or fears,
blocks.zh_text: 担忧、疑虑或恐惧占据时，表现就会变差，

blocks.en_text: instead of focusing its attention on performing the task at hand.
blocks.zh_text: 而不是把注意力集中在完成眼前的任务上。

blocks.en_text: When relevant and irrelevant thoughts compete for the same attention,
blocks.zh_text: 当相关的想法和不相关的想法争夺同一份注意力时，

blocks.en_text: something has to give.
blocks.zh_text: 总有一方要让步。

blocks.en_text: The brain can only process so much information at once.
blocks.zh_text: 大脑一次只能处理这么多信息。

blocks.en_text: Tasks that challenge working memory,
blocks.zh_text: 那些挑战工作记忆的任务——

blocks.en_text: the mental “scratch pad” we use
blocks.zh_text: 工作记忆就是我们用来

blocks.en_text: to temporarily store phone numbers and grocery lists,
blocks.zh_text: 临时记住电话号码和购物清单的“草稿纸”——

blocks.en_text: are especially vulnerable to pressure.
blocks.zh_text: 特别容易受到压力的影响。

blocks.en_text: In a 2004 study, a group of university students
blocks.zh_text: 在2004年的一项研究中，一组大学生

blocks.en_text: were asked to perform math problems,
blocks.zh_text: 被要求做数学题，

blocks.en_text: some easy, others more complex and memory-intensive.
blocks.zh_text: 有些题简单，有些题更复杂、更费记忆。

blocks.en_text: Half the students completed both problem types with nothing at stake,
blocks.zh_text: 一半学生在没有任何利害关系的情况下完成了两种题目，

blocks.en_text: while the others completed them when calm and under pressure.
blocks.zh_text: 而另一半学生则在平静时和压力下各完成一次。

blocks.en_text: While everyone did well on the easy problems,
blocks.zh_text: 虽然每个人在简单题上都做得不错，

blocks.en_text: those who were stressed performed worse
blocks.zh_text: 但那些感到压力的学生

blocks.en_text: on the more difficult, memory-intensive tasks.
blocks.zh_text: 在更难、更费记忆的题目上表现更差。

blocks.en_text: Explicit monitoring theories make up the second group of explanations
blocks.zh_text: 外显监控理论构成了压力下发挥失常的

blocks.en_text: for choking under pressure.
blocks.zh_text: 第二类解释。

blocks.en_text: They’re concerned with how pressure
blocks.zh_text: 这类理论关注的是压力

blocks.en_text: can cause people to overanalyze the task at hand.
blocks.zh_text: 如何让人过度分析眼前的任务。

blocks.en_text: Here, the logic goes that once a skill becomes automatic,
blocks.zh_text: 这里的逻辑是，一旦某项技能变得自动化，

blocks.en_text: thinking about its precise mechanics interferes with your ability to do it.
blocks.zh_text: 去想它的具体动作机制反而会干扰你完成它的能力。

blocks.en_text: Tasks we do unconsciously seem to be most vulnerable to this kind of choking.
blocks.zh_text: 我们无意识完成的任务似乎最容易出现这种发挥失常。

blocks.en_text: A study on competitive golfers compared their performance
blocks.zh_text: 一项针对竞技高尔夫球手的研究比较了他们的表现：

blocks.en_text: when instructed to simply focus on putting as accurately as possible,
blocks.zh_text: 一种情况是让他们只专注于尽可能准确地推杆，

blocks.en_text: versus when they were primed to be acutely aware
blocks.zh_text: 另一种情况是事先让他们高度留意

blocks.en_text: of the mechanics of their putting stroke.
blocks.zh_text: 自己推杆动作的机制。

blocks.en_text: Golfers usually perform this action subconsciously,
blocks.zh_text: 高尔夫球手通常是无意识地完成这个动作的，

blocks.en_text: so those who suddenly tuned in to the precise details of their own moves
blocks.zh_text: 所以那些突然关注起自己动作精确细节的人

blocks.en_text: also became worse at making accurate shots.
blocks.zh_text: 在准确投篮方面也变得更差了。

blocks.en_text: Choking may not be inevitable for everyone though.
blocks.zh_text: 不过，发挥失常对每个人来说也许并非不可避免。

blocks.en_text: Research suggests that some are more susceptible than others,
blocks.zh_text: 研究表明，有些人比其他人更容易受影响，

blocks.en_text: especially those who are self-conscious,
blocks.zh_text: 尤其是那些自我意识强、

blocks.en_text: anxious,
blocks.zh_text: 容易焦虑、

blocks.en_text: and afraid of being judged negatively by others.
blocks.zh_text: 以及害怕被别人负面评价的人。

blocks.en_text: So, how can we avoid choking when it really counts?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，在真正关键的时刻，我们怎样才能避免发挥失常呢？

blocks.en_text: First, it helps to practice under stressful conditions.
blocks.zh_text: 首先，在压力环境下练习会有帮助。

blocks.en_text: In a study on expert dart players,
blocks.zh_text: 在一项针对资深飞镖选手的研究中，

blocks.en_text: researchers found that those who hadn’t practiced under stress
blocks.zh_text: 研究人员发现，那些没有在压力下练习过的人

blocks.en_text: performed worse when anxious,
blocks.zh_text: 在焦虑时表现更差，

blocks.en_text: compared to those who had become accustomed to pressure.
blocks.zh_text: 相比之下，那些已经习惯压力的人则表现更好。

blocks.en_text: Secondly, many performers extol the virtues of a pre-performance routine,
blocks.zh_text: 其次，许多表演者都推崇表演前固定流程的好处，

blocks.en_text: whether it’s taking a few deep breaths,
blocks.zh_text: 无论是做几次深呼吸、

blocks.en_text: repeating a cue word,
blocks.zh_text: 重复一个提示词，

blocks.en_text: or doing a rhythmic sequence of movements.
blocks.zh_text: 还是做一套有节奏的连续动作。

blocks.en_text: Studies on golfing, bowling, and water polo
blocks.zh_text: 针对高尔夫、保龄球和水球的研究

blocks.en_text: find that short rituals can lead to more consistent
blocks.zh_text: 发现，简短的固定仪式能让表现更稳定、

blocks.en_text: and accurate performance under pressure.
blocks.zh_text: 在压力下更准确。

blocks.en_text: And thirdly, researchers have shown
blocks.zh_text: 第三，研究人员已经表明，

blocks.en_text: that having an external focus on the ultimate goal
blocks.zh_text: 把注意力放在最终目标这个外部焦点上

blocks.en_text: works better than an internal focus,
blocks.zh_text: 比放在内部焦点上更有效，

blocks.en_text: where someone is tuned into the mechanics of what they’re doing.
blocks.zh_text: 也就是把注意力集中在动作的具体机制上。

blocks.en_text: A study of experienced golfers revealed that those who hit chip shots
blocks.zh_text: 一项针对经验丰富的高尔夫球手的研究显示，那些打切球时

blocks.en_text: while focused on the flight of the ball
blocks.zh_text: 把注意力放在球的飞行轨迹上的人

blocks.en_text: performed significantly better than those who focused on the motion of their arms.
blocks.zh_text: 表现明显好于那些把注意力放在手臂动作上的人。

blocks.en_text: So, perhaps we can modify that age-old saying:
blocks.zh_text: 所以，也许我们可以把那句老话改一改：

blocks.en_text: practice,
blocks.zh_text: 练习，

blocks.en_text: under pressure,
blocks.zh_text: 在压力下，

blocks.en_text: with focus,
blocks.zh_text: 带着专注，

blocks.en_text: and with that glorious end goal in sight,
blocks.zh_text: 并且心中想着那光辉的最终目标，

blocks.en_text: makes perfect.
blocks.zh_text: 才能做到完美。
